hints.title: Monotonic Path Invariance
hints.text: Every coordinate step towards the target must be made regardless of path ordering, so every monotonic path costs the same.

hints.title: Non-Monotonic Inefficiency
hints.text: Moving away from the destination only adds strictly positive additional step costs, making deviation suboptimal.

hints.title: Direct Coordinate Range Sum
hints.text: Sum rowCosts along the direct row direction and colCosts along the direct column direction.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minCost(self, startPos: list[int], homePos: list[int], rowCosts: list[int], colCosts: list[int]) -> int:
        cost = 0
        r_step = 1 if homePos[0] >= startPos[0] else -1
        c_step = 1 if homePos[1] >= startPos[1] else -1

        r = startPos[0]
        while r != homePos[0]:
            r += r_step
            cost += rowCosts[r]

        c = startPos[1]
        while c != homePos[1]:
            c += c_step
            cost += colCosts[c]

        return cost
```

complexity.time: O(|startRow - homeRow| + |startCol - homeCol|) path cost accumulation
complexity.notes: Any monotonic route visits the exact same set of row and column intervals.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Graph shortest path algorithms like Dijkstra are unnecessary because all monotonic paths have identical minimum cost.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct interval sum avoids constructing graph edges or path priority queues.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should prove that moving strictly towards the home coordinates is optimal.
